name: Second Battle of Kosovo
summary: At the Second Battle of Kosovo (October 17–19, 1448), Hungarian regent János Hunyadi leads a large crusading force of Hungarians, Wallachians, and Polish volunteers against the Ottoman army of Sultan Murad II. The battle lasts three days; Vlad II of Wallachia withdraws his forces mid-battle, contributing to the defeat. The failure ensures Ottoman control of the Balkans and makes the fall of Constantinople (1453) a matter of when, not if. It is the last major attempt to roll back Ottoman power before the fall of Constantinople.

_quarry.structural_significance: Ends the last serious challenge to Ottoman Balkan dominance; makes the fall of Constantinople inevitable; demonstrates the impossibility of crusading success against the disciplined Ottoman military machine
